# Find Nuclei Viewer

> Browser-based viewer for OME-ZARR (OME-NGFF) microscopy data with GPU-accelerated rendering.

## What it does

Find Nuclei Viewer is a zero-install web application for viewing and annotating bio-image data in OME-ZARR format. It runs entirely in the browser. No data is uploaded to any server. The same viewer embeds in any web page or MyST article as an interactive figure, and can tell the hosting page how readers use it.

## Key capabilities

- Opens local ZARR files directly from disk (no upload, no server required)
- Opens a dataset zipped into one .ozx or .zip file, from disk or from its https:// or s3:// address. By address it reads only the parts it needs, by HTTP range requests (the server must allow CORS and range requests; S3, R2 and GCS do). Dropbox file links work as pasted, but they are not the best way to share data for viewing: Dropbox takes several seconds to answer each read, so opening a large image can take a minute or more. For data viewed often, use object storage (S3, R2, GCS) or any web server that supports range requests. Dropbox folder links, Google Drive, OneDrive and Proton Drive are not supported. Guide: https://find-nuclei.github.io/docs/guides/remote-urls.html#zipped-datasets
- Shape annotations (polygons, lines, points, distance measurements) with browser-local persistence
- Export annotations as CSV spreadsheet or GeoJSON
- Segmentation label overlays from ZARR or local/network drive
- Multi-channel fluorescence visualization with custom colors and intensity ranges
- Per-channel histograms and auto-contrast (2%–98% percentile)
- Z-projection (max, mean, min intensity) with configurable Z-range
- 3D view of a z-stack: WebGPU volume rendering (MIP or Composite) next to orthogonal XY, XZ and YZ planes with a shared crosshair. Up to four channels at once, a per-channel opacity ramp in Composite, and annotations and label images that carry between 2D and 3D (labels show as a surface per object or as a coloured volume, in the colours set in 2D). Reads OME-NGFF anatomical orientation (RFC-4): axes labelled superior/inferior, left/right, anterior/posterior, and a radiological (medical) plane convention. Opens from a URL, a local folder (Chrome and Edge), an .ozx or .zip file, or a token-protected store, in a desktop browser with WebGPU. Guide: https://find-nuclei.github.io/docs/guides/3d-rendering.html
- High-Content Screening (HCS) plate navigation with well picker and field grid
- GPU-accelerated multi-resolution tiled rendering via deck.gl WebGL
- Shareable deep links: the URL tracks zoom, position, channels and Z-slice in real time
- Reads OME-NGFF 0.6, the current spec, plus 0.3, 0.4 and 0.5, including sharded stores
- Handles images exceeding 100,000 pixels in either dimension

## Embedding in articles and web pages

- Two lines of HTML: `<script src="https://find-nuclei.github.io/embed/v1/viewer.js"></script>` once per page, then `<find-nuclei-viewer url="https://example.org/image.zarr"></find-nuclei-viewer>` for each figure
- MyST and Curvenote articles (Elemental Microscopy and other Curvenote sites): an `any:bundle` directive pointing at `https://find-nuclei.github.io/embed/v1/widget.mjs`; every JSON key becomes an attribute of the viewer
- Attributes set the starting view and look: `x`, `y`, `zoom`, `z`, `t`, `channels`, `invert`, `grayscale`, `background`, `autoplay`, `fps`, and `id` to name the figure
- The viewer's toolbar has an Embed button that turns the current view into HTML or MyST code
- Reader interactions: each embedded viewer dispatches a `fn-viewer:interaction` DOM event (bubbles, composed, so it leaves shadow roots) for every reader action: ready, pan, zoom, channel, z, t, play, pause, visible, hidden. Each event carries the full view at that moment: centre, zoom, visible bounds, z-slice, timepoint, channels and contrast, and the figure's `id`
- The viewer sends nothing anywhere itself. The hosting page collects the events with its own analytics and owns the data. Use it to measure reader engagement with interactive figures, time on figure, and where readers look
- Guides: https://find-nuclei.github.io/docs/guides/embedding.html and https://find-nuclei.github.io/docs/guides/reader-analytics.html
- Live demos: https://find-nuclei.github.io/publications.html, https://find-nuclei.github.io/publications/myst-embed.html, https://find-nuclei.github.io/publications/embed-events.html

## Who it's for

Researchers and scientists working with microscopy data: digital pathology, spatial biology, high-content screening, confocal microscopy, light-sheet imaging, electron microscopy, super-resolution microscopy, spatial transcriptomics, live-cell imaging. Authors, journals, preprint servers and data portals that publish interactive microscopy figures.

## Technical details

- Format: OME-ZARR (OME-NGFF) v0.3, v0.4, v0.5 and v0.6. In 0.6: coordinate systems with scale and translation, labels, plates and time-lapses. Scenes and affine transforms are not rendered yet
- HCS instrument plates, opened from their own files without conversion, by URL, s3:// or a local folder: Opera Phenix plates exported by Harmony (V5 Index.idx.xml, V6 Index.xml) and Yokogawa CellVoyager CV8000 and CV7000 measurement folders. Together they cover most JUMP Cell Painting plates in the Cell Painting Gallery. Guides: https://find-nuclei.github.io/docs/guides/opera-phenix-plates.html and https://find-nuclei.github.io/docs/guides/yokogawa-plates.html
- Browsers: Chrome and Edge open everything, including dataset folders from disk. Firefox and Safari open web links and zipped datasets (.ozx or .zip) from disk or by address
- Rendering: deck.gl with WebGL, multi-resolution tiled loading
- 3D rendering: WebGPU, loaded only when a user switches to 3D. Desktop browsers only. The image needs more than one z-section and opens from a URL, a local folder (Chrome and Edge), an .ozx or .zip file (from disk or its address), or a token-protected store. A link with `mode=3d` opens in 3D, and a copied 3D link carries the camera, render mode, layout and Surface labels. Details: https://find-nuclei.github.io/docs/guides/3d-rendering.html
- Privacy: all processing is client-side, no server backend required
- No account or installation required
